title: Akrill
description: Akrill, the acrylic paint look, is pigment as a plastic skin on the world: thick ridges, poster edges, high chroma, paint that still looks wet. Color sits on top: if it soaked in, you shot a wash.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Pop, a kids' myth, a poster that came alive: graphic shapes, a face still modeled, wet highlights on the paint itself. Canvas is gallery oil.
Ink riot is airborne liquid. Akrill is toy and poster matter.
It is the wrong tool for a period oil portrait, and the wrong tool if the color went watercolor-thin. Acrylic should look like plastic paint.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Eye height, 35mm to 50mm, lock-off. Hard or hard-soft studio key so ridges catch a wet highlight.
Ask for thick acrylic, high chroma, graphic shapes, modeled face. Prompt: Acrylic look on [Subject], thick plastic color, poster edges, paint that still looks wet.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Dick Tracy's spot color and makeup sit on faces like poster pigment. Pop-art cinema treats paint as candy.
Borrow the plastic color, not a frame.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: Thin watercolor, or a mash with Canvas oil. The tell is soaked-in color and no ridges.
Fix it: thick acrylic, poster edges, wet plastic highlights.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Akrill in film?
An acrylic-matter look: thick plastic color, poster edges, wet pigment sitting on the world. It is paint as object, not a wash.
Akrill vs Canvas
Canvas is oil and tooth, gallery stock. Akrill is acrylic ridges and poster chroma. If it looks like candy plastic, you are on akrill. If you see canvas weave, you wanted canvas.
When should I use Akrill?
Pop, toys, posters that come alive. Skip period oil and thin watercolor.
How do I prompt Akrill for AI image or video?
Hard key, then: Acrylic look on [Subject], thick plastic color, poster edges, paint that still looks wet. Demand ridges and wet highlights. Keep the face modeled.
